next_research_stage: New version/prospective protocol only. Do not reopen v0.31.

overall_conclusion.primary_mechanistic_failure: utility selector/intervention gate remained effectively inactive; utility probabilities stayed near 0.5 and active intervention remained zero across clean, graded, and catastrophic conditions.
overall_conclusion.statement: AEGIS v0.31 preserved clean performance but failed all five prospectively frozen scientific hypotheses. The calibrated evidence selective-intervention mechanism did not establish graded robustness, mismatch-transition improvement, combined-mechanism superiority, utility selectivity, or evidence-utility alignment.
overall_conclusion.successor_direction: A successor may investigate why the learned utility objective is non-discriminative or poorly optimized, but must be introduced under a new prospective protocol/version. v0.31 itself must not be retrained or retuned.

release.basis: scientific lifecycle complete with frozen negative results and clean regression suite

scientific_synthesis.interpretation: The calibrated selective-intervention design did not materially damage clean validation performance relative to the frozen safeguards.
The primary controller did not improve graded corruption robustness over the stable-reference baseline under the prospective H1 gate.
The calibrated controller did not establish superior mismatch-transition behavior relative to the frozen comparators.
Combining calibration and utility selection did not meet the prospectively frozen superiority requirements over either ablation.

The utility selector remained effectively centered near its initialization and produced zero active intervention across the evaluated corruption strata. The principal v0.31 mechanism therefore did not learn a useful intervention boundary.
The frozen H5 bands did not establish usable evidence-to-utility alignment; no post-exposure rebinning is permitted.
